q: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by ____ in 1820.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by Oersted in 1820.

q: When a straight wire carrying a current was placed above a compass needle, the needle was ____.
e: When a straight wire carrying a current was placed above a compass needle, the needle was deflected. Deflected is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the magnetic field due to the current flowing through the wire can be found by using the ____.
e: The direction of the magnetic field due to the current flowing through the wire can be found by using the right-hand rule. Right-hand rule is what this statement is using.

q: Imagine the wire to be grasped in the right hand with the ____ pointing along the wire in the direction of the current.
e: Imagine the wire to be grasped in the right hand with the thumb pointing along the wire in the direction of the current. Thumb is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the ____ will give the direction of the magnetic field.
e: The direction of the fingers will give the direction of the magnetic field. Fingers is what this statement is using.

q: The magnetic lines of force around the wire carrying a current are ____ around the wire and they are in the plane perpendicular to the wire.
e: The magnetic lines of force around the wire carrying a current are closed circular loops around the wire and they are in the plane perpendicular to the wire. Closed circular loops is what this statement is using.

q: A solenoid is a ____ of wire, which has a magnetic field inside and in its vicinity when a current flows through it.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire, which has a magnetic field inside and in its vicinity when a current flows through it.

q: The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a ____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a bar magnet.

q: When viewing one end of the solenoid, that end will be a south pole if the current is seen flowing in a ____ direction and north pole if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of the solenoid, that end will be a south pole if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction and north pole if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction.

q: If you hold the thumb, the first finger and the second finger of your left hand ____ to each other, with the first finger in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of the electric current, then the thumb will point in the direction of the motion along which the force acts.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. If you hold the thumb, the first finger and the second finger of your left hand mutually perpendicular to each other, with the first finger in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of the electric current, then the thumb will point in the direction of the motion along which the force acts.

q: When a ____ moves across a magnetic field it experiences a force.
e: When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field it experiences a force. Charged particle is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of force on that particle is ____ to those of $B$ and $v$.
e: The direction of force on that particle is perpendicular to those of B and v. Perpendicular is what this statement is using.
